column1:
Incorporating Beige Book insights tempers the FOMC’s “solid” growth characterization. District reports indicate modest, mixed expansion: consumer-oriented spending was flat to softer in several areas, while business services demand held up. Nonresidential construction increased in some regions, but commercial real estate—especially office—remains a drag, notwithstanding signs of stabilization and a pickup in office demand in New York City. Labor markets continued to ease: firms reported slower hiring, lower turnover, and some layoffs; wages are still rising but at a cooler pace. Prices are still increasing, but nonlabor input costs have declined in some Districts, reinforcing ongoing disinflation. Overlaying SLOOS, banks’ tighter standards and softer business loan demand should further restrain capex and hiring, muting the impulse from the 25 bp cut even as QT continues.

Net tone: cautiously positive on growth and inflation progress but less upbeat than a macro-only read, with downside risks to activity from restrictive credit and CRE offset by some regional stabilization and business optimism.
